lessons.title: Museum Volunteer Briefing
lessons.learningObjective: Follow task assignments and a changed meeting point in a volunteer briefing.

lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “family day” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “guide visitors” only with the meaning stated here.

lexicalTargets.meaning: set up places for practical tasks
lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “prepare activity tables” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “team leader” only with the meaning stated here.

activities.prompt: Which detail changed in the recording?

options.label: The detail stated in sentence three
A detail not mentioned in the recording

answer.text: Blue badge volunteers will guide visitors to the new science gallery.

activities.feedback: Use the exact changed detail rather than a plausible topic word.

activities.prompt: Write the second sentence exactly as you hear it.

answer.text: The briefing will start in the education room, not the front hall.

activities.feedback: Check content words, function words and the stated detail.

activities.prompt: Retrieve the fourth sentence without opening the transcript.

answer.text: Green badge volunteers should prepare activity tables near the cafe.

activities.feedback: Opening the answer makes this attempt coaching-only.

activities.prompt: Shadow the final two sentences with thought-group pauses.

answer.text: Green badge volunteers should prepare activity tables near the cafe. Meet your team leader at eight forty-five so the doors can open at nine.

activities.feedback: Aim for rhythm and intelligibility; this is coaching, not independent evidence.

activities.prompt: Retell the practical outcome in two sentences.

answer.text: Mention the main change and the required action, using family day where suitable.

activities.feedback: Retell remains coaching-only without an independent evaluator.

lessons.title: Temporary Bus Route Change

Use “temporary stop” only with the meaning stated here.

activities.prompt: Which detail changed in the recording?

options.label: The detail stated in sentence three

lessons.title: Restoring Dunes with Flexible Barriers
lessons.learningObjective: Recognise how a restoration method changes wind and sand movement.

lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “establish roots” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “settles around” only with the meaning stated here.

lexicalTargets.meaning: change where material is worn away
lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “redirect erosion” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “working with local movement” only with the meaning stated here.

activities.prompt: State the passage’s central claim in one sentence.

answer.text: Recognise how a restoration method changes wind and sand movement.

activities.feedback: A strong answer preserves the scope of the passage.

activities.prompt: Which expression best preserves “establish roots”?

answer.text: develop a stable root system

activities.feedback: Match meaning and claim strength, not just topic.

activities.prompt: Identify a plausible statement that the passage does not establish.

answer.text: A broad universal claim that removes the passage’s stated limitation.

activities.feedback: Distractors often repeat vocabulary while changing scope or causality.

activities.prompt: Find the sentence that limits the main claim and explain its function.

answer.text: The limiting sentence prevents the evidence from supporting a broader conclusion.

activities.feedback: Look for contrast markers and cautious reporting verbs.

activities.prompt: Write 70–90 words using “settles around” to evaluate the passage.

answer.text: A complete paragraph should state a claim, cite a passage detail and preserve one limitation.

activities.feedback: This follow-up is coaching-only until independently evaluated.

lessons.title: Comparison and Contrast
lessons.learningObjective: Build precise comparisons without changing the reference group.

lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “compared with” only with the meaning stated here.

lexicalTargets.meaning: in contrast to the preceding clause
lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “whereas” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “a similar proportion” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “considerably lower than” only with the meaning stated here.

activities.prompt: Recall a precise meaning for “compared with”.

answer.text: examined in relation to

activities.feedback: Keep the strength and grammatical role of the expression.

activities.prompt: Choose the expression matching: in contrast to the preceding clause.

answer.text: whereas

activities.feedback: Use the meaning note rather than surface similarity.

activities.prompt: Write one academic sentence using “compared with”.

answer.text: The sentence should use the expression in its stated sense and register.

activities.feedback: Check collocation, grammar and claim strength.

activities.prompt: Write 70–90 words using “compared with” and “whereas”.

answer.text: The paragraph should connect both expressions coherently without changing their meanings.

activities.feedback: Prefer a clear claim and one supporting example.

activities.prompt: Paraphrase “a similar proportion” without increasing certainty.

answer.text: roughly the same share

activities.feedback: Preserve modality and scope.
